title: Bug:Route Not Installed in FIB After Connected Route Deletion
author: archanajpatel-collab
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

When a route prefix is programmed in the RIB by both a connected route and a static route, the connected route is preferred by the RIB and installed in the FIB. After the connected route is deleted, the RIB correctly selects the static route; however, the static route is not installed in the FIB.


### Steps to Reproduce

-Configure Ethernet264 with IP 10.0.0.1/24 (creates connected route for 10.0.0.0/24)
sudo config interface ip add Ethernet264 10.0.0.1/24

-Configure Ethernet268 with IP 20.0.0.1/24 (for static route next-hop)
sudo config interface ip add Ethernet4 20.0.0.1/24

-Bring up both interfaces
sudo config interface startup Ethernet264
sudo config interface startup Ethernet268

-Add static route for 10.0.0.0/24 via 20.0.0.2
sudo config route add prefix 10.0.0.0/24 nexthop 20.0.0.2

sudo config interface shutdown Ethernet264

Static route 10.0.0.0/24 via 20.0.0.2 is not installed in FIB.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual Behavior: Static route 10.0.0.0/24 via 20.0.0.2 is not installed in FIB. 
Expected Behavior:  Static route 10.0.0.0/24 via 20.0.0.2 is expected to be installed in FIB. 

### Relevant log output

```shell
The prefix affected by the issue is 10.0.0.0/24. After triggering an interface shutdown, the connected route is removed and an update for the 10.0.0.0/24 prefix is sent. The prefix is subsequently deleted upon the next update from the MRIB.

2026-01-23 08:43:50.078 [DEBG] zebra: [W3XNK-8CC35] rib_meta_queue_add: (default:254):10.0.0.0/24: queued rn 0x558fb5042060 into sub-queue Connected Routes mq size 8
2026-01-23 08:43:50.087 [DEBG] zebra: [PM9ZJ-07RCP] 0:10.0.0.0/24 Dplane route update ctx 0x558fb507a220 op ROUTE_UPDAT
2026-01-23 08:43:50.087 [DEBG] zebra: [GW4S4-NE28R] rib_meta_queue_add: (default:254):10.0.0.0/24: rn 0x558fb5042060 is already queued in sub-queue Connected Routes
2026-01-23 08:43:50.087 [DEBG] zebra: [W3XNK-8CC35] rib_meta_queue_add: (default:254):10.0.0.0/24 (MRIB): queued rn 0x558fb4bbfea0 into sub-queue Connected Routes mq size 9
2026-01-23 08:43:50.087 [DEBG] zebra: [GW4S4-NE28R] rib_meta_queue_add: (default:254):10.0.0.0/24: rn 0x558fb5042060 is already queued in sub-queue Connected Routes
2026-01-23 08:43:50.088 [DEBG] zebra: [PM9ZJ-07RCP] 0:10.0.0.0/24 Dplane route update ctx 0x558fb5081b00 op ROUTE_DELET
```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell
SONiC OS Version: 12 (202505)
FRRouting (version 10.3)
```

### Attach files (if any)

[RouteUpdateIssue.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24812731/RouteUpdateIssue.txt)

This issue is likely introduced by the commit https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/3bff65abc75e952a15b98666e7271189ac28a2bc in FRR.
Prior to this commit, routes from MRIB were blocked from flowing through the dataplane, which resulted in:
   Routes never being marked as installed
   MRIB nexthop tracking (NHT) not functioning for routes learned after the tracking request

The commit changed behavior by allowing MRIB routes to flow through the dataplane pipeline, but they are not sent to:
   Linux kernel
   FPM (Forwarding Plane Manager)

The commit modified upstream FRR’s dplane_fpm_nl.c to filter routes from MRIB. SONiC uses dplane_fpm_sonic.c, and this filter was not added there.

Fix: Skipping routes from MRIB in dplane_fpm_sonic.c resolves the issue.

Is this a known issue OR is there an open PR addressing it?

Thanks @archanajpatel-collab .
The image version we're using is based on [phoenixwing](http://phoenixwing.com.cn/code): both SONiC and FRR from 08192025 master.

From the Zebra side, its behavior has been confirmed correct in both of our testbeds.
From the FPM side, we have tested this problem by using two modes: "fpm use-next-hop-groups" or NOT, and FPM's behavior is correct with correct events from zebra in our testbed for both modes.

#### Mode 1: Default setting
By default, we use "fpm use-next-hop-groups" mode. The connected routes' NHGs would not be installed in FPM due to FRR setting them as NEXTHOP_GROUP_INITIAL_DELAY_INSTALL:
```
if (RIB_SYSTEM_ROUTE(re))
			SET_FLAG(nhe.flags, NEXTHOP_GROUP_INITIAL_DELAY_INSTALL);
```
This leads to skipping zebra_nhg_install_kernel():
```
/* FRR's code */
static enum zebra_dplane_result
dplane_nexthop_update_internal(struct nhg_hash_entry *nhe, enum dplane_op_e op)
{
	enum zebra_dplane_result result = ZEBRA_DPLANE_REQUEST_FAILURE;
	int ret;
	struct zebra_dplane_ctx *ctx = NULL;

	/* Obtain context block */
	ctx = dplane_ctx_alloc();

	ret = dplane_ctx_nexthop_init(ctx, op, nhe);
	if (ret == AOK) {
		if (CHECK_FLAG(nhe->flags, NEXTHOP_GROUP_INITIAL_DELAY_INSTALL)) {
			UNSET_FLAG(nhe->flags, NEXTHOP_GROUP_QUEUED);
			UNSET_FLAG(nhe->flags, NEXTHOP_GROUP_REINSTALL);
			SET_FLAG(nhe->flags, NEXTHOP_GROUP_INSTALLED);

			dplane_ctx_free(&ctx);
			atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&zdplane_info.dg_nexthops_in,
						  1, memory_order_relaxed);

			return ZEBRA_DPLANE_REQUEST_SUCCESS;
		}

		ret = dplane_update_enqueue(ctx);
	}
```
This seems not a correct behavior and causes the connected routes to not show up in "show ip fib", **but it's another problem**. Even though we cannot directly observe the transition from connected to static route, we can still verify the behavior by checking Redis DB logs.
- Step 1: After configuring the static route, we shut down the connected one's interface (Ethernet4):

     ```
     L>* 20.0.0.1/32 is directly connected, Ethernet0, weight 1, 01:00:49
     ```

   - Check swss.rec: Ethernet4 is SET down in PORT_TABLE and 10.0.0.0/24 (static) is SET in ROUTE_TABLE

     ```
     admin@P3:/var/log/swss$ tail -n 100 swss.rec | grep -B 3 "10.0.0"
     ...
     2026-02-17.20:55:54.213387|PORT_TABLE:Ethernet4|SET|admin_status:down 
     2026-02-17.20:55:54.257759|ROUTE_TABLE:10.0.0.0/24|SET|nexthop:20.0.0.2|ifname:Ethernet0|nexthop_group:|protocol:0xc4
     ```

MRIB nexthop tracking (NHT) not functioning for routes learned after the tracking request

Linux kernel
FPM (Forwarding Plane Manager)

The commit modified upstream FRR’s dplane_fpm_nl.c to filter routes from MRIB. SONiC uses dplane_fpm_sonic.c, and this filter was not added there.

linkedPullRequests.title: [dplane_fpm_sonic]: Skip MRIB routes to prevent FIB route deletion
linkedPullRequests.author: Bojun-Feng
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/25173

FRR commit https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/3bff65abc75e952a15b98666e7271189ac28a2bc changed behavior to allow MRIB routes through the dataplane pipeline, and upstream's `dplane_fpm_nl.c` was updated to filter them (See this [permalink](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/blob/7d94895937ce058c654ef27ea39dd1bd55d75844/zebra/dplane_fpm_nl.c#L1785-L1806)). SONiC's `dplane_fpm_sonic.c` was not updated with the same filter, so MRIB ROUTE_DELETE events reach fpmsyncd and delete valid unicast routes from APP_DB.

#### How I did it

Added a `SAFI_MULTICAST` check in `fpm_nl_process()` within `dplane_fpm_sonic.c`, mirroring the upstream FRR fix in `dplane_fpm_nl.c`. Route operations (`ROUTE_DELETE`, `ROUTE_INSTALL`, `ROUTE_UPDATE`) with `SAFI_MULTICAST` are skipped and not enqueued to fpmsyncd.

#### How to verify it

See https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/25173#issuecomment-4186559462 for issue replication instructions. After the fix, `show ip fib` should not miss `10.10.0.0/24`.

#### Description for the changelog

Skip MRIB routes in dplane_fpm_sonic to prevent FIB route deletion when connected routes are withdrawn.
